questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities and cultural and cultural heritage of the city. The many courses on ecocritical and interdisciplinary approaches was a big +

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really happy to be able to take some courses with students from UMPRUM. This opened up a lot of doors for me!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: This bureaucratic system with mobility online and learning agreements and preliminary approvals - it is all very confusing and frustrating.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a bunch of Q+A sessions upon arrival.  This helped.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Go on different sites on facebook! There are many english-friendly sites. Also used the FAMU DAMU+ page to search for likeminded students

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a great way infto becoming part of an environment with people that are not necessarily  as new to town as you. A great way of tapping into an already established group of more or less local people

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Signing up was easy enough but from then this long Kafkaesque online maze started. I really think you need to reshape the system into something easier than Mobility. Or at least do some videos or meet-ups or Q+A's for the whole procedure

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I ended up at my host university's student office many times. thank god for their help!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most of the classes I wanted turned out to be cancelled.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for a lot of courses, then attend all of them the first week and choose the ones that your gut tells you to

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is hard to say something general cause it depends so much on the teacher. but generally (!) the czechs were less attentive at class than I am used to. This made it less lively. Also the courses are much smaller than at UCPH (3--5 ECTS each) so the wingspan is just smaller.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More free, less attached to curriculum. But also less in-depth

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ecocritical approaches to American Poetry
Ecofeminism
Contemporary Art
English - Close Reading of contemporary feminists
Mimesis and Materiality in US poetry
International Experimental Fiction
Basic Czech

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Mimesis and Materiality in US poetry - just anything with Stephan Delbos, he is absolutely great!

Also the Contemporary Art course to meet people from other faculties. -a lot of artists from UMPRUM

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cell service and bike repair. Also had a small fire in my apartment which made some expenses..

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cell service is quite expensive compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not follow any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some of my friends did climbing and yoga

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit all the museums and jazz bars! And be sure to see the final exhibitions at AVU and UMPRUM. Also the philharmonic at Rudolfinum is super cheap for students. A musT!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The cultureplace Punctum

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None I think

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The engagement in their surroundings. The deeply cultural DNA of so many of the locals

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be sure to get a class with Stephan Delbos
- You are allowed to rollerskate inside the faculty in the evenings if you smile gently at the security guards
- The library at Clementinum is way better than the one at the faculty of arts. You pay a little but it is worth it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a great swimming spot down South at the tram stop Nadrazi Branik. The river is clean enough there!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other people. Getting really good friends. Broadening my academic horizons.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my loved ones at home. Fortunately you can both fly, ride a bike, car or train to Prague!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
